stories.teaser: Technion makes green hydrogen and a valuable chemical, at 98% efficiency
stories.headline: Technion researchers make green hydrogen and a valuable industrial chemical at 98% efficiency
stories.why: A membrane-free method published in Nature Communications; a US patent application has been filed.
texts:
Clean fuel, plus a bonus.

Technion researchers led by Prof. Avner Rothschild found a way to split water into green hydrogen while producing epoxide, an ingredient used in plastics, coatings and medicines, instead of plain oxygen. Both reactions ran at 98% efficiency.

“We approached this challenge by rethinking the water-splitting process,” he says.

#Israel #Technion #CleanEnergy #Hydrogen

98% efficiency, for two products at once.

A Technion team has developed a membrane-free method that produces green hydrogen and the industrial chemical epoxide together, with only 2% of the electrical charge lost to other reactions. The researchers say the current density is compatible with large-scale industrial electrolysis. Published in Nature Communications.

#Israel #Technion #CleanEnergy #Hydrogen

What if making clean fuel also made something valuable on the side?

That’s the idea behind a new Technion method that turns water and renewable electricity into green hydrogen and epoxide, a building block for polymers, adhesives and pharmaceuticals.

“By optimizing the entire system, we succeeded in producing both hydrogen and epoxide efficiently,” says Dr. Guilin Ruan.

#Israel #Technion #CleanEnergy #Hydrogen
stories.og_title: Technion develops breakthrough method to produce green hydrogen and epoxide

stories.headline: A 300-meter stretch of Jerusalem’s 2,000-year-old aqueduct is uncovered
stories.why: The Lower Aqueduct carried water about 21 km to the Temple Mount; it will be displayed in a new neighborhood.
texts:
2,000 years ago, Jerusalem got its water by gravity alone.

The Israel Antiquities Authority has uncovered a 300-meter stretch of the Lower Aqueduct in southern Jerusalem. The channel dropped only about one meter per kilometer on its roughly 21 km route to the Temple Mount.

“The aqueduct is an engineering marvel,” says IAA Jerusalem District Archaeologist Amit Re’em.

#Israel #Archaeology #Jerusalem #History

300 meters uncovered. About 21 km long. Around 2,000 years old.

The Israel Antiquities Authority has exposed a section of Jerusalem’s Lower Aqueduct, which brought spring water to the Temple Mount. It was used on and off until about 100 years ago. Planners want to display the remains along a promenade in a new neighborhood.

#Israel #Archaeology #Jerusalem #History

How did ancient Jerusalem get its water?

Through an aqueduct so gently sloped it dropped about one meter per kilometer. A 300-meter stretch has just been uncovered.

“The thought that about 2,000 years ago they managed to bring water to Jerusalem this way is astonishing,” says IAA archaeologist Amit Re’em.

#Israel #Archaeology #Jerusalem #History
stories.og_title: 300-meter stretch of ancient aqueduct uncovered during planning for new Jerusalem neighborhood

stories.teaser: New Israel Museum show explores childhood in ancient Israel
stories.headline: New Israel Museum exhibition explores childhood in the ancient Land of Israel
stories.why: “Tiny Footprints” brings together hundreds of artifacts from 11 institutions, from prehistory to the first millennium CE.
texts:
What was it like to be a child 3,000 years ago?

The Israel Museum’s new exhibition, “Tiny Footprints: Childhood in the Ancient Land of Israel,” gathers hundreds of artifacts from 11 institutions: a 3,000-year-old pottery pull toy shaped like an otter, tiny hand axes sized for small hands, and figurines carrying a child’s fingerprints.

“Mothers are mothers wherever they are, and children act like children,” says curator Tali Sharvit.

#Israel #IsraelMuseum #Archaeology #Culture

Hundreds of artifacts. 11 institutions. Thousands of years of childhood.

“Tiny Footprints” at the Israel Museum in Jerusalem traces children’s lives from prehistory to the end of the first millennium CE, with toys, feeding vessels, a Byzantine writing tablet and a mosaic of a boy in a short tunic. It runs through the end of February.

#Israel #IsraelMuseum #Archaeology #Culture

Did ancient kids play with toys like ours?

They did. A new exhibition at the Israel Museum in Jerusalem shows a pottery otter on wheels from the 11th century BCE and much more.

“What’s amazing about these toys is how similar they are to today,” says curator Tali Sharvit.

#Israel #IsraelMuseum #Archaeology #Culture
stories.og_title: From birth to play, new exhibition explores childhood in ancient Israel

stories.teaser: Israeli scientists find how cancer cells survive chemotherapy
stories.headline: Ben-Gurion University scientists find ‘guardian proteins’ that help cancer cells survive chemo
stories.why: Dr. Aeid Igbaria’s lab identified two proteins, DNAJB12 and DNAJB14, in a study published in Redox Biology.
texts:
Why do some cancers survive chemotherapy? Israeli scientists may have found part of the answer.

Dr. Aeid Igbaria’s lab at Ben-Gurion University of the Negev identified two “guardian proteins” that open an emergency valve, letting cancer cells survive the stress of treatment. When the bonds holding them together break, the guardians fall apart, clearing the way for the cancer cell to self-destruct.

#Israel #Science #CancerResearch #BGU

2 proteins. 1 emergency valve that keeps cancer cells alive.

Researchers at Ben-Gurion University of the Negev found that the proteins DNAJB12 and DNAJB14 help cancer cells survive chemotherapy stress. The work, done in human cell lines and published in Redox Biology, offers a new target for tackling chemo resistance.

#Israel #Science #CancerResearch #BGU

Cancer plays chess. Now scientists know one of its moves.

“When we talk about cancer, it’s like we are talking about playing chess,” says Dr. Aeid Igbaria of Ben-Gurion University. His lab found two “guardian proteins” that help cancer cells survive chemotherapy, research that may help future treatments overcome resistance.

#Israel #Science #CancerResearch #BGU
stories.og_title: How cancer cells survive chemo: Israeli researchers find 'guardian proteins' protect tumors

stories.teaser: Raz Hershko wins bronze at the World Judo Championships
stories.headline: Israel’s Raz Hershko wins bronze at the World Judo Championships
stories.why: In Baku, the +78 kg judoka won four bouts, including the bronze match by ippon in golden score.
texts:
Another world medal for Israel.

Judoka Raz Hershko won bronze in the +78 kg category at the World Judo Championships in Baku. After wins over opponents from Chinese Taipei, Estonia and Brazil, she clinched the medal by ippon against Croatia’s Helena Vuković in golden score.

Proud of her.

#Israel #Judo #Sport #TeamIsrael

4 wins. 1 world bronze.

Israel’s Raz Hershko took bronze in the women’s +78 kg division at the World Judo Championships in Baku, beating Croatia’s Helena Vuković by ippon in golden score in the bronze-medal bout. Earlier she defeated opponents from Chinese Taipei, Estonia and Brazil.

#Israel #Judo #Sport #TeamIsrael

What does it take to win a world medal in golden score?

Ask Raz Hershko. After four minutes of regulation time, the Israeli judoka beat Croatia’s Helena Vuković by ippon in golden score to win bronze at the World Judo Championships in Baku. It was her fourth win of the tournament in the +78 kg category.

#Israel #Judo #Sport #TeamIsrael
stories.og_title: Raz Hershko Wins Bronze Medal at the World Judo Championships

stories.teaser: Weizmann AI rebuilds what you see from a brain scan
stories.headline: Weizmann Institute AI reconstructs what people see from their brain scans
stories.why: Brain-IT adapts to a new person with about one hour of scan data, instead of the 40 hours earlier methods needed.
texts:
Imagine a computer drawing the picture you’re looking at, just from your brain activity.

A team led by Prof. Michal Irani at Israel’s Weizmann Institute built Brain-IT, an AI that reconstructs images people view from fMRI scans. It needs only about one hour of scan data from a new person, instead of 40. One day, it could help paralyzed people communicate.

#Israel #Science #AI #Neuroscience

40 hours of brain scans, cut to about 1.

The Weizmann Institute’s Brain-IT system reconstructs the images people look at from fMRI brain scans, and adapts to a new person with about an hour of data. On data from four volunteers, it outperformed 10 other methods on 7 of 8 standard image-similarity measures. Presented at ICLR 2026.

#Israel #Science #AI #Neuroscience

Can AI see what you see?

Researchers at Israel’s Weizmann Institute, led by Prof. Michal Irani, built a system that turns brain scans into pictures of what a person is viewing. It is especially good at capturing layout, color and shape, and needs far less data than earlier methods.

#Israel #Science #AI #Neuroscience
stories.og_title: This AI Reconstructs What You're Looking at From a Brain Scan

stories.teaser: Weizmann study maps how menopause changes the whole body
stories.headline: Weizmann study of over 1 million women maps how menopause changes the whole body
stories.why: 300 million lab results analyzed: sudden shifts in 52 of 90 health measures. Published in Nature Medicine.
texts:
Menopause affects far more than most of us realize, and now there’s data to show it.

Prof. Uri Alon’s team at Israel’s Weizmann Institute analyzed more than 300 million lab results from over 1 million women. They found sudden changes in 52 health measures around menopause, including bone, liver, kidney and cholesterol markers.

“Our study extends the window for potential preventive care to almost a decade before menopause,” he says.

#Israel #WomensHealth #Science #Menopause

300 million lab results. Over 1 million women. 52 measures that shift suddenly.

Weizmann Institute researchers, working with Clalit Health Services and Israeli hospitals, used US and Israeli data to map how menopause changes the body. Hormonal shifts start speeding up more than a decade before the final period. Published in Nature Medicine.

#Israel #WomensHealth #Science #Menopause

When does menopause really begin to change a woman’s body?

Earlier than you might think. A Weizmann Institute study of over 1 million women found that sex hormone changes start accelerating more than a decade before the final period, with sudden shifts in dozens of health markers.

That could open a much longer window for prevention, through diet and exercise.

#Israel #WomensHealth #Science #Menopause
stories.og_title: Menopause triggers sudden changes throughout the body, Israeli study finds

stories.teaser: Israel returns 22 ancient Greek artifacts to Greece
stories.headline: Israel returns 22 ancient Greek artifacts to Greece, the first such return between the two countries
stories.why: Pottery from the 8th to 4th centuries BCE, seized in a 2020 investigation, handed over in Athens.
texts:
Some treasures belong at home.

Israel has returned 22 ancient Greek artifacts, pottery from the 8th to 4th centuries BCE decorated with scenes from Greek mythology, to Greece. The Israel Antiquities Authority seized them in a 2020 investigation into illegal antiquities trading. It is the first such return between the two countries.

#Israel #Greece #Heritage #Archaeology

22 ancient vessels, roughly 2,300 to 2,800 years old, back where they came from.

The Israel Antiquities Authority, working with Israel Police and the Israel Tax Authority, seized the pottery in a 2020 raid on illegal antiquities traders near Tel Aviv. This week it was handed over at the National Archaeological Museum in Athens, the first return of its kind from Israel to Greece.

#Israel #Greece #Heritage #Archaeology

What happens to stolen antiquities after they’re seized?

Sometimes, they go home. Israel just returned 22 Greek ceramic vessels, some painted in black-figure and red-figure styles, to Greece.

“Every return of antiquities to their country of origin also carries a broader moral and symbolic meaning,” said Greek Culture Minister Lina Mendoni.

#Israel #Greece #Heritage #Archaeology
stories.og_title: Israel returns 22 ancient Greek artifacts seized in police raids near Tel Aviv

stories.teaser: Dozens of endangered butterfly rays gather off Israel’s coast
stories.headline: Dozens of endangered butterfly rays gather in the shallows off Israel’s northern coast
stories.why: A species critically endangered in the Mediterranean, filmed by nature rangers off Shavei Zion.
texts:
Sometimes the sea surprises you.

During a routine snorkeling survey off Shavei Zion in northern Israel, Israel Nature and Parks Authority rangers found dozens of spiny butterfly rays gliding over the sandy seabed. In the Mediterranean, this species is critically endangered.

“Sometimes we think we need to travel far to see the wonders of nature, but they’re right here, in our Mediterranean Sea,” says ranger Shay Kabsa.

#Israel #Nature #Ocean #Wildlife

Dozens of rays from a species critically endangered in the Mediterranean, in one spot.

Israel Nature and Parks Authority marine rangers filmed spiny butterfly rays gathering in the shallow waters off Shavei Zion, near Nahariya. Experts think it may be linked to courtship and reproduction. These rays are protected under Israeli law, and the public is asked to keep its distance.

#Israel #Nature #Ocean #Wildlife

Have you ever seen the seabed come alive?

Israeli marine rangers did, when dozens of endangered spiny butterfly rays appeared beneath them off the northern coast.

“We don’t need to touch nature to experience it. Sometimes all we need to do is float quietly and watch,” says ranger Ziv Neder.

#Israel #Nature #Ocean #Wildlife
stories.og_title: Rare sight off Israel's coast: dozens of endangered butterfly rays gather in shallow waters

stories.teaser: Magen David Adom adds 96 new ambulances for its 96th year
stories.headline: Magen David Adom unveils 96 new ambulances to mark 96 years
stories.why: Donated by supporters in seven countries, joining a fleet of about 2,000 ambulances.
texts:
96 years of saving lives, celebrated with 96 new ambulances.

Magen David Adom, Israel’s national emergency medical service, unveiled 96 new ambulances at its headquarters in Ramla. They were donated by supporters in the United States, Canada, France, the UK, Switzerland, Belgium and Australia, and will help shorten response times across Israel.

#Israel #MDA #SavingLives #Gratitude

96 new ambulances. 7 donor countries. A fleet of about 2,000.

Magen David Adom marked its 96th year by unveiling 96 new ambulances, given by its international Friends associations. They join a fleet of roughly 2,000 vehicles, expanding emergency coverage across Israel and helping crews reach patients faster.

#Israel #MDA #SavingLives #Gratitude

What’s the best way to celebrate a 96th birthday?

For Magen David Adom, it’s 96 new ambulances, donated by friends around the world.

“While 96 is a mature age, Israel’s national emergency medical service is young and strong…” says MDA Director-General Eli Bin. The new vehicles join a fleet of about 2,000 ambulances across the country.

#Israel #MDA #SavingLives #Gratitude
stories.og_title: Magen David Adom unveils 96 new ambulances to mark 96 years

stories.teaser: Rangers rescue four ibex trapped in a Negev canyon
stories.headline: Rangers rescue four ibex trapped in a remote Negev stream
stories.why: Israel Nature and Parks Authority inspectors freed all four, one with the help of a wooden ramp.
texts:
A happy ending in the desert.

Tourists spotted four ibex stuck on a slippery, remote stretch of the Vardit Stream in the Negev and alerted the Israel Nature and Parks Authority. Inspectors first waited to see if the animals could free themselves. When they couldn’t, the team stepped in, and all four made it out.

#Israel #Nature #Wildlife #Negev

4 trapped ibex. 4 rescued.

Israel Nature and Parks Authority staff freed four wild mountain goats stuck in the Vardit Stream in the Negev Desert. Two were helped out directly, one climbed to safety on a wooden ramp the rescuers built, and specialists freed the last one.

#Israel #Nature #Wildlife #Negev

How do you rescue a stuck mountain goat?

In Israel’s Negev, rangers tried everything: they climbed in to help two ibex, built a wooden ramp that a third used to climb out on its own, and brought in specialists for the fourth. All thanks to tourists who spotted them and called for help.

#Israel #Nature #Wildlife #Negev
stories.og_title: Rescuers help free four mountain goats trapped in Negev

stories.teaser: Hebrew University’s Haim Sompolinsky wins the Dirac Medal
stories.headline: Israeli brain scientist Prof. Haim Sompolinsky wins the Dirac Medal
stories.why: The ICTP prize recognizes his work linking physics, the brain and artificial intelligence.
texts:
A top physics honor for an Israeli who helped explain how brains learn.

Prof. Haim Sompolinsky of the Hebrew University has won the Dirac Medal and Prize from the International Centre for Theoretical Physics in Trieste. His work helped establish theoretical neuroscience and explains how neural networks learn and store memories, in brains and in computers.

#Israel #Science #Neuroscience #AI

One of theoretical physics’ top honors goes to an Israeli.

Prof. Haim Sompolinsky, professor emeritus at the Hebrew University’s Edmond and Lily Safra Center for Brain Sciences, shares the ICTP’s Dirac Medal and Prize, recognized for linking physics with the study of the brain and artificial intelligence.

#Israel #Science #Neuroscience #AI

How do neural networks, in our heads and in our computers, learn and remember?

Israeli physicist Prof. Haim Sompolinsky helped answer that, and has now won the Dirac Medal and Prize.

“Haim has fundamentally changed the way we understand intelligence, both natural and artificial,” says Hebrew University president Prof. Tamir Sheafer.

#Israel #Science #Neuroscience #AI
stories.og_title: Israeli professor wins prestigious international physics award
